In mathematics, the '''Zarhin trick''' is a method for eliminating the polarization of  [[abelian variety|abelian varieties]] ''A'' by observing that the abelian variety ''A''<sup>4</sup>&nbsp;×&nbsp;''Â''<sup>4</sup> is principally polarized.  The method was introduced by {{harvs|txt|last=Zarhin|year=1974}} in his proof of the [[Tate conjecture]] over [[global field]]s of positive [[characteristic (algebra)|characteristic]].
